dossiers.claim: Across the selected passages, mirror moon repeatedly changes source markers that distinguish Shiki’s present narrating ‘I,’ the named figure Tohno Shiki, involuntary bodily impulse, and later reflective judgment. The local errors do not all move in one grammatical direction, but they recurrently make divided or morally self-questioning focalization read as a single, more settled voice.

dossiers.cumulative_effect: An English reader receives a Shiki who is more psychologically unitary, more certain about his own motives, and at several decisive points less explicitly implicated in what his body, desire, or later judgment is doing. That alters the route-wide tension between action, compulsion, witness, and blame.

dossiers.heading: Shiki: focalization, self-division, and moral agency
dossiers.method_note: Every card begins with a final public finding whose Japanese and mirror moon bytes are frozen. The local agency, naming, modality, or rhetorical error is direct evidence; the claim that their recurrence changes Shiki’s work-wide focalization is a bounded editorial inference tested against accepted counterexamples.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not claim that every Shiki line is mistranslated, that every first-person sentence is dissociative, or that English must mechanically preserve Japanese pronouns. Its claim is limited to passages where naming, agency, modality, repetition, or explicit self-judgment carries demonstrable force.

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve when the narration treats Shiki as an observed or named self rather than an undivided ‘I’?
subsections.name: Dissociated focalization and the named self

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English keep bodily compulsion, perception, and deliberate action assigned to the same agents and faculties as the source?
subsections.name: Impulse, body, and divided agency

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve how Shiki judges his own identity, belonging, responsibility, and capacity for violence?
subsections.name: Self-conception, belonging, and moral judgment

dossiers.claim: In a distributed set of comic, intimate, and lethal scenes, mirror moon repeatedly recalibrates Arcueid’s affect or the terms of her nonhuman existence: jokes lose their operative premise, ordinary happiness is abstracted or reassigned, and predatory force or reciprocal attachment changes degree, target, or logic. The result weakens the source’s deliberate coexistence of innocence, appetite, danger, and chosen affection.

evidence.japanese:
「そんな事より、志貴はどうして闘ったりしたの？
　志貴はわたしに協力してくれるって言ったけど、一人で闘うとは言わなかったわ」
　じろり、とアルクェイドは俺を睨みつけてくる。
　……それは一人で危険な真似をした俺の身を案じている―――
「もう、ずるいわよ志貴！
　わたしに内緒で、一人でそんな楽しそうなコトするなんて！」
――――というワケでもなさそうだった。
evidence.japanese_excerpt: わたしに内緒で、一人でそんな楽しそうなコトするなんて！
evidence.label: s161
evidence.mirror_moon:
"More importantly, why did you fight?
You said you'd team up with me, but you never said you'd fight by yourself."
She glares at me.
…… She seems seriously concerned about my safety----
"That's not fair Shiki!
Keeping it a secret, having all that fun by yourself!"
----or not.
evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: Keeping it a secret, having all that fun by yourself!

counterexamples.reason: The English preserves the comic reversal: Shiki initially interprets Arcueid's glare as concern for his safety, only for her to complain that he enjoyed a dangerous fight without her.
counterexamples.title: Arcueid's apparent concern still pivots into hunter's envy

evidence.japanese:
「――――そうなのかな。
わたし、誰かに感情を持つなんて初めてだからよく解らないけど……」
　と、アルクェイドは少しのあいだだけ黙り込んで、顔をあげた。
「……その、志貴はわたしのこと、嫌いなのかな……？」
　なんて事を、聞いてきた。
evidence.japanese_excerpt: 誰かに感情を持つなんて初めて
evidence.label: s165
evidence.mirror_moon:
"----Is that so?
This is the first time I've ever felt emotion towards someone, so I don't really understand it myself……"
After being quiet for a few moments, she raises her head.
"…… Um, Shiki, do you hate me……?"
And asks me such a question.
evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: This is the first time I've ever felt emotion towards someone

counterexamples.reason: The English keeps the extraordinary premise behind her uncertainty: she has never before possessed feelings directed toward another person, so she cannot interpret whether anger means hatred.
counterexamples.title: Arcueid's first emotion toward another person remains explicit

evidence.japanese:

たった少し、本当にたったの七日間だけなのに。
　……わたしは正しいのかなって。
　だって、すごく楽しいんだもの。
こうしてるのが、生きているっていうのが、ただそれだけで嬉しいなんて、今まで考えたこともなかった」
evidence.japanese_excerpt: 本当にたったの七日間だけなのに
evidence.label: s176
evidence.mirror_moon:
"----But now, I don't know anymore.
For just a brief time… really, only seven days.
…… I started to wonder if I really was right?
Because it was so fun.
Doing this, living like this, I never thought until now how happy it could make me."
evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: really, only seven days

counterexamples.reason: The English preserves both the tiny seven-day interval and Arcueid's discovery that merely doing this and being alive can make her happy, the central change that frightens her.
counterexamples.title: Arcueid's seven purposeless days and joy in living remain explicit

counterexamples.reason: The English keeps the crucial correction from a shared joke to something Arcueid can no longer stop, along with her trembling voice and talon-like grip.
counterexamples.title: Arcueid's joke turning into frightening loss of control is preserved

evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: when I waited for you, the one who I madly thought about, I felt happy.

counterexamples.reason: Despite awkward syntax, mirror moon retains the paradox that Arcueid's intense wait for the person she hated was happy, supporting the transition from hatred to human anticipation.
counterexamples.title: Waiting for Shiki becomes Arcueid's first remembered happiness

evidence.japanese:
「……あいつ、一人だからさ。
なんか、ほっとけないんだ。
たぶん、理由はそんなものだよ」

真面目に答えてください遠野くん。
……そんな理由じゃ、わたしは納得できません」

evidence.japanese_excerpt: あいつは今まで一人で、楽しいっていう事がいっぱいあるって事も知らなくて
evidence.label: s199
evidence.mirror_moon:
"…… Because she's by herself.
I can't just leave her alone.
I think that's why."
"----That's a lie.
You can't risk your life because of that.
Please answer seriously, Tohno-kun.
…… I can't understand that kind of reason."
"No, it really is my reason.

Always, almost foolishly isolated.
Isn't it too lonely?
I won't allow such a meaningless life.
So----"
evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: Until now she's been alone, she never even knew what it was like to have fun.

evidence.japanese:
「……ただ、教えてやりたかった。
　あいつはあんなに楽しそうに笑うけど、そんなのは誰にでも手に入れられるものなんだって、教えてやりたかった。
　世の中にはもっと―――もっと、それこそつまらない悩みなんて消しとぶぐらい楽しい事があるんだって、何回でも連れまわしたかった。
　当たり前のことを、当たり前のように感じられるように―――あいつを、幸せにしてやりたかった」
　いつでも、本当に笑っていられるように。
　アルクェイドの笑顔が、好きだったから。
evidence.japanese_excerpt: 当たり前のことを、当たり前のように感じられるように
evidence.label: s199
evidence.mirror_moon:
"…… I just, wanted to tell her.
Even though she smiles like she's enjoying herself immensely, I wanted to show her anyone can have that.
I wanted to show her over and over this world has more----even more enjoyable things, enough to make any hardships seem like nothing.
To be able to feel all the normal things as something normal----I wanted to make her happy."
So she can truly smile all the time.
Because I like Arcueid's smile.
evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: To be able to feel all the normal things as something normal

counterexamples.reason: Unlike the earlier reversal at 02595, this long confession preserves Shiki's wish that Arcueid learn purposeless everyday pleasures, experience ordinary things as ordinary, and become happy through his own hands.
counterexamples.title: Shiki's ordinary-happiness philosophy is sustained in the later confession

dossiers.cumulative_effect: The English Arcueid is less consistently legible as a person discovering ordinary reciprocal life while remaining categorically nonhuman. Comic abrasiveness, inexperienced pleasure, lethal capacity, and the growth of mutual concern become more generic and less causally connected.

examples.reason: Arcueid playfully quotes Shiki's repeated な sounds and asks what all the stammering is. mirror moon treats the line as though she simply failed to hear him, deleting the joke and her teasing response to his panic.
examples.title: Arcueid's imitation of Shiki's stammer becomes a request to repeat himself

evidence.japanese:

　傷が塞がっていない状態で眠ると身体の抵抗力が落ちてしまって、傷がますます悪化するっていうコトだと思う。
　睡眠が回復してくれるのは疲れだけで、傷や病気は治してくれないだろ。
だから、とりあえず手当てをするまでは眠らないようにするんだ」
「―――へえ。
うん、それってその通りよ志貴」
　アルクェイドは嬉しそうに笑う。

evidence.mirror_moon:
"It's absurd but do it.
I've heard your bodily functions weaken when you sleep.
I think if you sleep with open wounds, your immune system will get weak and your wound will get even worse.
Sleeping will only help your tiredness, not heal your wound.
So for now, at least don't sleep until I get back."
"----Really?
Okay, I'll do that Shiki."
Arcueid smiles happily.
…… As expected, Arcueid's thought process is completely a mystery.
evidence.mirror_moon_highlight: Okay, I'll do that Shiki.

examples.reason: Arcueid cheerfully confirms that Shiki's improvised medical reasoning is exactly right. mirror moon instead has her agree to obey him, changing both the speech act and the joke that her inhuman physiology happens to validate his dubious theory.
examples.title: Arcueid's confirmation becomes compliance

examples.reason: Arcueid cannot believe humans knowingly make useless routines into daily shackles or constraints. mirror moon changes that negative burden into a positive purpose, 'something you live for'; Shiki then repeats the mistranslated phrase as if she had described motivation rather than bondage.
examples.title: A daily shackle becomes something to live for

dossiers.heading: Arcueid: affect, ordinary happiness, predation, and comic voice
dossiers.method_note: The local errors are source-bounded findings. Their distribution across ordinary conversation, combat, philosophical exposition, and intimacy supports the cumulative characterization argument; accepted localizations test whether the pattern has been overstated.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not claim that Arcueid is simply innocent, simply predatory, or uniformly mistranslated. It also does not demand literal transfer of every joke. It addresses passages where the source supplies a specific emotional, comic, philosophical, or physical relation that the English materially changes.

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve the premise, social awkwardness, and affective discovery carried by Arcueid’s jokes and ordinary desires?
subsections.name: Comic encounter and ordinary pleasure

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English retain the source’s target, degree, and governing rule when Arcueid acts or reasons as a vampire?
subsections.name: Predation and nonhuman rules

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve the bodily and visual cues through which Arcueid’s jealousy, distress, pleading, or destabilization becomes legible?
subsections.name: Affective legibility

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve who wants, accepts, protects, or understands whom as the relationship changes?
subsections.name: Intimacy and reciprocity

dossiers.claim: Across school, Church, combat, and intimate scenes, mirror moon repeatedly alters the distinctions among Ciel’s cultivated school persona, her competence as an executor, the religious and moral terms through which she understands herself, and the irony of her closeness to Shiki. These are local semantic and register failures whose recurrence makes her shifting roles less sharply articulated.

dossiers.heading: Ciel: professional competence, religious register, intimacy, and irony
dossiers.method_note: Direct cards establish local mistranslations of action, religious terminology, speech act, or emotional logic. The conclusion about role architecture is cumulative and expressly bounded by successful scenes where mirror moon preserves persona, competence, and vulnerability.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not claim that every polite line is false performance, that Ciel never loses control, or that all religious language admits only one English solution. It is limited to places where action, institutional meaning, address, irony, or emotional logic is textually recoverable.

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve Ciel’s chosen social performance and the comic or relational mechanics that expose it?
subsections.name: School persona and comic diction

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English keep Ciel’s professional action, Church concepts, and moral or doctrinal distinctions intact?
subsections.name: Executor competence and religious register

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve the double meaning, emotional direction, and self-knowledge in Ciel’s closeness to Shiki?
subsections.name: Intimacy, irony, and the concealed self

dossiers.claim: Across household, school, confrontation, and intimate scenes, mirror moon repeatedly changes the grounds of Akiha’s control: disciplined authority becomes generic severity, family and heir obligations lose their specific constraints, and moments of vulnerability or desire shift agency, degree, or causal logic. The pattern does not make her simply softer; it makes the tensions within her authority less coherent.

dossiers.heading: Akiha: control, vulnerability, desire, and family obligation
dossiers.method_note: The public cards directly establish local changes in action, family status, emotion, or sexual agency. The claim about their combined effect on Akiha’s authority is interpretive and is limited by counterexamples where difficult prickliness, obligation, and vulnerability remain intact.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not claim that Akiha’s harshness is always protective, that her authority is merely an act, or that every compressed English line is wrong. It concerns passages where the source explicitly states who controls, fears, desires, inherits, orders, or yields.

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve the inherited duties, bodily appetite, and practical decisions through which Akiha maintains control?
subsections.name: Control, appetite, and heir obligation

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve the event, bodily response, or emotional inference that interrupts Akiha’s control?
subsections.name: Vulnerability beneath composure

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English retain the direction, degree, and bodily or relational logic of Akiha’s desire?
subsections.name: Desire and chosen attachment

dossiers.claim: In scenes distributed across household service, memory, illness, and intimacy, mirror moon repeatedly substitutes explicit emotional labels or altered actions for Hisui’s reserve and nonverbal perception, and changes who initiates, permits, resists, or understands bodily contact. The recurrent issue is not quietness alone but the source’s use of quietness as active information and choice.

dossiers.heading: Hisui: reserve, perception, bodily boundaries, and chosen agency
dossiers.method_note: The local gesture, agency, referent, and consent findings are direct. The route-wide account of reserve as perception and choice is cumulative, tested against accepted cases where mirror moon successfully leaves silence implicit or reconstructs difficult bodily and servant-role language.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not equate reserve with passivity, claim that Hisui never speaks directly, or treat every natural English expansion as an error. It is limited to scenes where gesture, silence, service language, touch, consent, or chosen action has a recoverable source structure.

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve what Hisui notices or communicates through timing, gaze, silence, and bodily sign rather than invented explanation?
subsections.name: Reserve and nonverbal perception

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English preserve whether service is duty, promise, deference, practical care, or a chosen relation?
subsections.name: Service, trust, and household role

subsections.bounded_question: Does the English keep bodily response, coercion, refusal, permission, and self-directed action distinct?
subsections.name: Bodily boundaries and chosen agency

dossiers.claim: Across the far-side routes, mirror moon repeatedly disturbs the distinctions among Kohaku’s performed smile, her claimed doll-like selflessness, calculated manipulation, coerced history, bodily pain, and moments of genuine desire or attachment. The errors vary locally, but together they make it harder to tell when the text is exposing a role, assigning culpability, or allowing a suppressed self to become perceptible.

dossiers.heading: Kohaku: performance, coercion, calculation, pain, and selfhood
dossiers.method_note: Direct findings establish altered action, physical response, motive, or identity language. The claim about Kohaku’s performed and chosen selves is cumulative; accepted counterexamples demonstrate that mirror moon sometimes preserves the same ambiguity, coercion, and rhetorical structure with considerable skill.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not absolve Kohaku of calculation, treat every smile as false, or reduce her to abuse history. It claims only that specific distinctions among performance, coercion, agency, pain, and selfhood are repeatedly changed at passages where the Japanese makes them consequential.

dossiers.claim: In a narrower but coherent group of school, night, and confrontation scenes, mirror moon changes Satsuki’s social isolation, forms of address, remorse, and the involuntary bodily logic of her vampirism. The selected errors recurrently shift whether she is forgotten, compelled, guilty, rationalizing, or reaching toward Shiki, rather than merely changing the surface wording of a short subplot.

dossiers.method_note: The local address, temporality, bodily-state, and moral-logic findings are direct. Their combined account of Satsuki’s tragedy is a bounded inference, checked against accepted lines that preserve her threat, remorse, continued desire to live, and the route’s typographic staging.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not claim full route-scale density, that Satsuki lacks predatory choice, or that every address form needs Japanese morphology in English. The character has a smaller source footprint, so the case is intentionally capped at sixteen independently useful findings rather than padded with branch duplicates or loosely associated vampire lore.

dossiers.claim: Across recurring school and friendship scenes, mirror moon repeatedly loses the operative mechanics of Arihiko’s puns, garbled language, pop-cultural references, and boasts, while several action and speech-act errors change what he sees, asks, does, or tells Shiki. The combined effect weakens both his character-specific comic diction and his practical role as a social and informational counterweight.

dossiers.heading: Makihisa and the Tohno household: inheritance, abuse, secrecy, and roles
dossiers.method_note: The cards establish local facts about roles, records, places, and acts. The claim that their accumulation weakens the household architecture is editorial inference tested against counterexamples where mirror moon keeps such distinctions clear.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not reduce the household to a legal chart, treat every domestic paraphrase as an error, or infer abuse beyond what the selected Japanese passages state.

subsections.purpose: It is probative because a legal, genealogical, or succession relation is changed rather than merely renamed.
subsections.title: Inheritance, kinship, and legal identity

subsections.purpose: It belongs in this subsection because the English changes an abusive act, concealment, or Makihisa's causal responsibility.
subsections.title: Makihisa, abuse, and concealment

subsections.purpose: It supports the dossier by altering who serves, commands, manages, trusts, or belongs within the household hierarchy.
subsections.title: Service, authority, and household roles

subsections.purpose: It matters here because a spatial or institutional fact anchors the family's remembered and concealed history.
subsections.title: Mansion space, memory, and institutional history

dossiers.claim: Across the route structure, mirror moon sometimes changes address, reciprocity, role, or speech act in ways that move characters closer, farther apart, or into a different hierarchy than the Japanese. The claim is falsifiable at each card by checking whether the cited relation and direction of intimacy survive.

dossiers.method_note: The local claims are direct comparisons of agency, consent language, anatomy, and sequence. The account of ethical and character effect is cumulative editorial inference, constrained by accepted cases where mirror moon naturalizes explicit material without changing its relations.

dossiers.heading: Violence, body horror, sensory prose, and euphemistic flattening
dossiers.method_note: The example cards reproduce frozen Japanese and mirror moon evidence exactly. Local titles, reasons, severities, and categories are direct adjudicated findings; the work-wide pattern and cumulative reader effect are editorial inferences bounded by the selected counterexamples. Membership does not increase the audit's headline finding count.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not claim that mirror moon always sanitizes violence, that greater explicitness is automatically better, or that every anatomical difference affects plot. The accepted counterexamples show passages where compression, idiomatic substitution, or graphic English preserves the scene.

dossiers.claim: mirror moon recurrently regularizes passages whose force depends on uncertainty about dreaming, waking, remembering, acting, or observing. It changes epistemic scope, mental subject, and transitions between states often enough across the routes to make Shiki's unstable focalization more settled than the Japanese.

coverage.recurrence_note: Repeated branch or route records are retained only when recurrence is part of the finding; unique examples and evidence occurrences are reported separately.

dossiers.cumulative_effect: Dreams and waking life become easier to separate, but the work's intended doubt about who perceives, remembers, desires, or acts is weakened. Memory recovery can arrive with different timing, dissociation can read as ordinary confusion, and images that should recur as evidence of a divided self lose their connective force.

dossiers.method_note: The example cards reproduce frozen Japanese and mirror moon evidence exactly. Local titles, reasons, severities, and categories are direct adjudicated findings; the work-wide pattern and cumulative reader effect are editorial inferences bounded by the selected counterexamples. Membership does not increase the audit's headline finding count.
dossiers.not_claiming: The dossier does not claim that every obscure dream sentence has one mandatory English solution, or that clarity is inherently unfaithful. It identifies only cases where source-bounded state, agency, memory, or uncertainty is materially changed, and it preserves successful clarifications as counterexamples.

dossiers.claim: The Japanese builds meaning through concrete literary images, recurring motifs, refrains, parallel clauses, and typographic structures. At the cited passages, mirror moon replaces those forms with generic explanation, different imagery, or unmarked prose. This dossier distinguishes one-off image loss from work-wide recurrence: only the callback, refrain, and repeated-form evidence supports claims about connections across scenes or routes.

dossiers.heading: Literary images, motifs, callbacks, and repeated structures
dossiers.method_note: The example cards reproduce frozen Japanese and mirror moon evidence exactly. Local titles, reasons, severities, and categories are direct adjudicated findings; the work-wide pattern and cumulative reader effect are editorial inferences bounded by the selected counterexamples. Membership does not increase the audit's headline finding count.
dossiers.not_claiming: This dossier does not demand lexical identity whenever an image recurs, nor does it treat every elegant variation as an error. It concerns documented cases where the image, callback, contrast, or parallel structure itself carries meaning that the English materially changes or drops.

dossiers.claim: mirror moon sometimes localizes jokes successfully, but a recurrent subset loses the trigger, misidentification, register clash, allusion, or speaker-specific logic that makes the Japanese funny. The resulting English may preserve a literal topic while no longer supplying the setup and payoff as a functioning joke.

dossiers.method_note: The example cards reproduce frozen Japanese and mirror moon evidence exactly. Local titles, reasons, severities, and categories are direct adjudicated findings; the work-wide pattern and cumulative reader effect are editorial inferences bounded by the selected counterexamples. Membership does not increase the audit's headline finding count.
dossiers.not_claiming: The dossier does not require literal transfer of unportable puns and does not treat inventive compensation as betrayal. Its accepted counterexamples include free English rewrites that recreate the comic mechanism; the criticism applies when neither the source mechanism nor an equivalent English one survives.

dossiers.claim: A work-wide subset of mirror moon's English contains two related but distinct failures. Some lines are independently defective English: malformed grammar, broken relations or referents, and nonidiomatic clause structure. Others are coherent English but materially flatten the Japanese voice, register, or rhythm. The first claim is testable in English alone; the second remains a bounded source-comparative editorial judgment.

dossiers.heading: English prose quality: grammar, rhythm, register, and semantic coherence
dossiers.method_note: The example cards reproduce frozen Japanese and mirror moon evidence exactly. Local titles, reasons, severities, and categories are direct adjudicated findings; the work-wide pattern and cumulative reader effect are editorial inferences bounded by the selected counterexamples. Membership does not increase the audit's headline finding count.
dossiers.not_claiming: The dossier does not claim that all unusual English is wrong, that every formal line is unnatural, or that mirror moon never writes effective prose. It distinguishes objective grammatical or semantic failures from cumulative editorial judgments and includes accepted renderings that are idiomatic despite departing from Japanese form.

dossiers.claim: Across the routes, mirror moon changes a recurring set of checkable facts: time and sequence, quantities, institutional roles, locations, medical details, and concrete objects. These are bounded source discrepancies, some locally small, whose accumulation makes causal and chronological reconstruction less reliable.

dossiers.heading: Choice language, typography, click boundaries, and formal staging
dossiers.method_note: The example cards reproduce frozen Japanese and mirror moon evidence exactly. Local titles, reasons, severities, and categories are direct adjudicated findings; the work-wide pattern and cumulative reader effect are editorial inferences bounded by the selected counterexamples. Membership does not increase the audit's headline finding count.
dossiers.not_claiming: The dossier does not demand visual identity between Japanese and English or treat every reflow as an error. English requires different line lengths, and many presentation changes are harmless. The claim is restricted to cases where form itself carries a choice, timing, contrast, sound, or staging function that materially changes.
